Final task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC6, AC7).

## Goal

Document the shared mineral kill-drop code in the GDD and confirm the whole project is green.

## Minimal implementation

- Update `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.1 to state that the kill-drop rule (small-asteroid single drop; non-asteroid 25–50 % re-drop) is implemented once in a shared helper used by both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`.
- Update §6.4's `GymMinerals` entry (and any relevant file-breakdown lines) to reflect the shared helper and the wired drop behaviour.
- Update `README.md` if it references the mineral layer.
- Run the full suite plus typecheck/build; triage any failure through the triage skill.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC6 — Documentation updated.** The GDD (§4.4.1 and §6.4) and the gym docstrings describe the shared mineral kill-drop code.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** `npm test` (the full suite) passes and `npm run typecheck` succeeds.
- The GDD §6.4 `GymMinerals` entry and any `README.md` mineral wording are consistent with the wired gym behaviour.
- `npm run build` succeeds and no balance or tuning values are changed.

- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — docstrings.

# Re-calibrate L4-L5 Generated Campaign Targets After Enemy Bullet-Speed Halving

## Problem statement

Halving every enemy `bulletSpeed` (AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ) lowered each firing archetype's `enemyDifficulty` score by ~0.5–1 point (weight 5/116). The difficulty sequencer's `argmin` now selects degenerate L4–L5 wave compositions — single-enemy firing waves — diverging from hand-tuned targets.

## Users

- **Player** — wants playable, escalating L4–L5 challenge, not trivial single-enemy waves.
- **Game designer** — wants the sequencer to track hand-tuned targets without re-balancing weights.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want L4–L5 campaign waves to present a meaningful, varied challenge, not degenerate single-enemy encounters.
- As a **game designer**, I want the sequencer's generated compositions to stay close to hand-tuned targets without re-tuning enemyDifficulty weights.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Non-degenerate compositions.** No L4–L5 generated wave consists of a single firing enemy. Compositions differ per wave (verified by enemyKey:count).
- **AC2 — Tight band to targets.** Each L4–L5 generated wave's measured `waveDifficulty` is within ±1.0 of its `targetDifficulty`. (Proposed resolution: the original "agreed band" is set to ±1.0, tighter than the existing per-wave CSV tolerance (~2.0), to prevent noticeable drift while allowing valid compositions.)
- **AC3 — No regression to base values.** `FACTOR_RANGES.bulletSpeed`, `FACTOR_WEIGHTS`, and every enemy `bulletSpeed` remain at the halved values from AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ.
- **AC4 — Full suite passes.** All tests pass, including new regression tests asserting AC1/AC2 and updated existing regression tests.

## Constraints

- Do not change `FACTOR_RANGES.bulletSpeed`, `FACTOR_WEIGHTS`, or enemy `bulletSpeed` values.
- No divergent copies between gym and game scenes.
- Minimal change: re-derive `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` or enhance `sequenceVariedWaves` — not both.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` (`src/core/configStore.ts`): L4 = [16, 24, 28], L5 = [45, 62].
- `difficulty-curves.csv` has mirrored L4–L5 targets.
- After halving: L4 waves changed from `scoutx18 / diverx18 / tankx18` (measured 22.9/31.3/36.2) to `swarmx1 / tankx1 / phaserx1` (measured 1.8/2.8/3.0).
- L5 w1: `phaserx12+scoutx18` (measured 41.1) → `phaserx12+swarmx1` (measured 29.1).
- Per-wave CSV tolerance is ~2.0 — the shift is within tolerance but composition quality is poor.

## Desired change

Re-derive L4–L5 `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` and `difficulty-curves.csv` rows against **post-halving** `enemyDifficulty` scores so `argmin` selects the same high-quality compositions. If target re-tuning alone is insufficient, enhance `sequenceVariedWaves` to prefer distinct archetypes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — Update `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` for L4/L5.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — Update mirrored L4–L5 targets.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — `sequenceVariedWaves` (if enhanced approach needed).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — New regression: L4–L5 `waveDifficulty` within ±1.0 of target; non-degenerate composition check.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts` — Gym-parity regression for AC1/AC2.
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — Read-only: inspect post-halving archetype scores.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep (low).** Re-tuning difficulty weights or reverting bullet-speed halving is documented as out of scope (parent Q3-A).
- **Approach uncertainty (medium).** Re-deriving targets may not fully restore quality if score ordering fundamentally changed; `sequenceVariedWaves` enhancement is the fallback, with more risk.
- **Regression-test churn (low).** Updating targets in `configStore.ts` and `difficulty-curves.csv` will require re-baselining existing pinned tests.
- **Assumption.** Re-deriving targets against post-halving scores is the preferred approach.
- **Assumption.** A ±1.0 difficulty-point tolerance is appropriate.

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent; completed).
- AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K — Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign (completed; prior retuning).
- AH-0MUQ5262M009UFLU — Implement dynamic, varied non-firing opening waves (completed; `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` precedent).
- AH-0MUNU6MGM007CI45 — Launch generated levels from the curve editor (completed; `sequenceVariedWaves` context).
- AH-0MUX3VFUW009M539 — Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks (sibling, non-blocking).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)
- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** – Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic into a shared core scene base class (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)

# Field power-up/weapon pickups must upgrade the item TEMPORARILY, not permanently

**Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical · **Stage:** intake_complete

## Problem statement

Every collection currently increments a **run-scoped, permanent** level for the
item, regardless of where it came from. A field pickup and a hold-full
(mineral-choice) reward both call the same permanent mutation path:

- Power-ups — `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect(id, permanent)` → `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent)`
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`).
- Weapons — `Player.equipWeapon(id, permanent)` unconditionally does
  `this._weaponLevels.set(weaponId, this.getWeaponLevel(weaponId) + 1)`
  (`src/entities/Player.ts`).

Consequently a field pickup permanently raises the level, and the level
persists after the timed effect expires. This is wrong: field pickups are
**temporary** improvements; only hold-full (mineral-choice) rewards are
**permanent**. Because the hold-full choice reads `getWeaponLevels()` /
`getPowerUpLevels()`, a temporary field pickup also currently inflates the
level offered by the next hold-full choice, which compounds the bug.

## Users and user story

> As the player, when I collect a power-up or weapon in the field I want its
> level to improve **only for the duration of the pickup's timed effect**, so
> that when the timer expires the item drops back to the level it had
> permanently earned. Permanent level improvements should come **only** from
> hold-full (mineral-choice) rewards.

Stakeholders: the player (correct, predictable power growth) and the producer /
balance owner (the hold-full choice must price the *permanent* level only).

## Required behaviour (worked examples)

Let `permanentGrants` = number of hold-full rewards taken for the item, and
`tempStacks` = number of field pickups collected during the current timed
window.

- An item is **owned/active** while `permanentGrants + tempStacks >= 1`.
- `permanentUpgradeLevel = permanentGrants - 1` (first hold-full reward = base
  level 0; each further hold-full reward = +1), i.e. lvl0 is the base tier.
- `effectiveLevel = permanentUpgradeLevel + tempStacks` when owned.
- A field pickup: `tempStacks += 1` **and** (re)starts the item's timed window
  (weapons `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` = 10 s; power-ups their existing timed duration,
  e.g. P3 shield 15 s). The window refreshes on each new field pickup.
- On window expiry: `tempStacks = 0`; `effectiveLevel` reverts to
  `permanentUpgradeLevel`. If `permanentGrants == 0` the item becomes inactive
  (no permanent level). Unconsumed consumable grants persist (see Resolved
  decisions 1).
- A hold-full reward: increments `permanentGrants` permanently, no timeout, and
  does **not** touch `tempStacks`.

Worked examples:

**A — field pickups only (no hold-full reward)**
1. Pick up P3 → lvl0 for x s.
2. Pick up P3 again before x s → lvl1 for x s (window refreshed).
3. x s expires → back to lvl0 / effect gone (no permanent level retained).

**B — hold-full reward then field pickups**
1. Take P3 from a hold-full choice → lvl0, permanent, no timeout.
2. Pick up P3 in the field → lvl1 for x s.
3. x s expires → back to lvl0 (permanent).
4. Take P3 from another hold-full choice → lvl1, permanent.

## Resolved decisions

1. **Unconsumed consumable grants on expiry (P6 Phase Shift charges / P7
   Teleport stacks).** Resolved: **(b) persist until consumed.** Expiry of the
   temporary window must **not** remove charges/teleports already granted; the
   player keeps them until used. The permanent/temporary level distinction
   still governs the *level* (and therefore future grants), but does not claw
   back an already-granted consumable. The producer asked us to *consider
   creating a second power-up type* for this consumable-grant distinction;
   that exploration is tracked as a non-blocking follow-up,
   [Consider a distinct power-up type for consumable temporary grants (P6/P7) (AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN)].
2. **`★ New` badge for a field-only item.** Resolved: **(a) permanent grants
   only.** Ownership for the hold-full choice derives from `permanentGrants`,
   so an item only ever picked up in the field still reads `★ New` until
   permanently acquired, and the choice never offers a level-up on a level
   that vanishes on expiry.
3. **Exact temporary window per weapon/power-up.** Resolved: **(a) reuse
   existing timed-effect durations** — weapons `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s),
   power-ups their configured duration (e.g. P3 shield 15 s), refreshed on each
   new field pickup. No new balance constants.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 — **Field pickups are temporary.** Collecting a power-up or weapon in the
  field raises the item's effective level by one only for the item's timed
  window and starts/refreshes that window. When the window expires, the
  temporary level is removed and the effective level reverts to the permanent
  level (or the item becomes inactive when there is no permanent level).
- AC2 — **Hold-full rewards are permanent.** Applying a `weapon-level` /
  `power-up-level` choice (and a first-time `weapon` / `powerup` choice)
  permanently raises the item's level with no timeout, independent of any
  active temporary window.
- AC3 — **Worked examples reproduce exactly.** Both example sequences (A and B)
  produce the states described above; tests assert the effective level and
  active/inactive state at each step.
- AC4 — **The hold-full choice reflects the permanent level only.** The
  `ChoiceContext` supplied by every launcher (`PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene`, `GymWeaponLeveling`) reports each item's **permanent**
  level, so a temporary field pickup never inflates the level-up offered (no
  offering "Lv.2" when only "Lv.1" is permanent). The change summary and
  `★ New` badge likewise derive from permanent level (ownership = permanent
  grants; Resolved decision 2).
- AC5 — **HUD/readouts show the effective level.** Any level readout (HUD
  weapon level, gym panels) shows `permanent + temporary` and updates when a
  temporary window expires.
- AC6 — **Run restart clears everything.** `reset()` / `resetWeaponLevels()` /
  `resetPowerUpLevels()` clear both permanent and temporary level state.
- AC7 — **Single source of truth.** The permanent/temporary distinction lives
  once (in `PowerUpLevelStore` for power-ups and in the `Player` weapon-level
  state), consumed identically by the game and every gym. No second,
  divergent copy of the level maths is added.
- AC8 — **Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene` and `GymWeaponLeveling`; the existing parity/equivalence
  guards continue to pass. Update the gym scenes in the same change per the
  repo gym↔game parity convention.
- AC9 — **Existing effect semantics preserved for hybrids and consumables.**
  - P9 Magnet / P10 Mineral Scoop remain hybrid: a field pickup is a
    refresh-only timed attraction (now with a temporary level); a hold-full
    reward is a permanent stack. The permanent stack count derives from
    `permanentGrants` and is unaffected by temporary levels.
  - P6 Phase Shift charges / P7 Teleport stacks keep their existing
    grant-then-consume semantics. Per Resolved decision 1, unconsumed grants
    from a temporary field pickup **persist until consumed** and are **not**
    removed when the window expires; tests assert that expiry removes the
    temporary *level* but leaves stored charges/teleports intact.
- AC10 — **Testing and validation.** Unit tests cover the worked examples, the
  temporary/permanent split, expiry revert, hold-full permanence, choice
  context, HUD readout and run reset. Full project test suite must pass with
  the new changes.
- AC11 — **Documentation updated.** GDD §4.4.2/§4.4.3 and the module doc
  comments (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`,
  `src/entities/Player.ts`) describe the temporary/permanent split, including
  the consumable-grant persistence rule. All related documentation is updated
  to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant
  wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Preserve the single mutation-point architecture (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K): the
  split is introduced **inside** `PowerUpLevelStore` and the `Player`
  weapon-level state, not in a parallel counter.
- No new balance constants: reuse `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` and existing per-power-up
  durations (Resolved decision 3).
- Preserve P9/P10 hybrid semantics and P6/P7 consumable semantics (AC9).
- Keep gym↔game parity; gyms and `PlayScene` run the same code (AC8).
- Do not scope-creep into the "distinct power-up type" redesign; that is the
  separate follow-up item AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN.

## Existing state

- `PowerUpLevelStore` tracks a single run-scoped `level` per power-up plus a
  separate `_permanentGrants` map; `collect()` always increments `level`,
  and only `permanent=true` also increments `_permanentGrants`. There is no
  temporary-vs-permanent split of `level`, and the "level persists across a
  timed effect expiring" contract is documented in the module header.
- `Player.equipWeapon(id, permanent)` always increments `_weaponLevels`; the
  `permanent` flag only controls whether the weapon is added to
  `_permanentWeapons` vs `_weaponTimers`. `_weaponTimers` expiry deletes the
  timer but never touches `_weaponLevels`.
- The hold-full choice consumes `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` /
  the store's `getLevels()`, so temporary field pickups currently inflate the
  offered level.

## Desired change

Split each item's level into a **permanent** component (hold-full grants only)
and a **temporary** component (field pickups, tied to the existing timed
window). Expose an effective level (`permanent + temporary`) for readouts and
the effect path, and a permanent level for the hold-full choice. Remove the
temporary component when the item's timed window expires (without clawing back
already-granted consumables). Clear both on run reset.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — consumable banking (Resolved decision 1b).** Persisting unconsumed
  temporary grants lets a player bank charges/teleports across an expiry.
  Mitigation: only the *level* reverts, so repeat field pickups still stop
  granting at the temporary cap once consumed; consumption remains bounded by
  play. Accepted by the producer at intake.
- **Risk — extra state complexity.** Tracking `tempStacks` per item alongside
  the timed effects risks a second, divergent counter. Mitigation: the split
  lives once, inside `PowerUpLevelStore` / `Player` (AC7), with no parallel
  counter.
- **Risk — gym↔game divergence.** A temp/permanent fix applied to only one
  caller would break parity. Mitigation: shared core plus the existing
  parity/equivalence guards (AC8).
- **Scope-creep risk.** The producer's "second power-up type" idea could pull
  this fix into a redesign. Mitigation: recorded as non-blocking follow-up
  AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN; explicitly out of scope here (Constraints).
- **Assumption.** `permanentUpgradeLevel = permanentGrants - 1` matches the
  existing level semantics (first grant = base level 0; each further grant
  = +1), mirroring `resolveWeaponAtLevel` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`.
- **Assumption.** The temporary window reuses the existing configured
  durations (`WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` 10 s; per-power-up durations) with no new
  tuning constants.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — Needs the `PowerUpLevelStore` split:
  permanent grants vs temporary field-pickup stacks; expose effective vs
  permanent levels; `collect(id, permanent)` routes the field pickup to the
  temporary component.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Needs the timed-effect lifecycle
  (`_startOrRefreshTimed`/expiry, `P9_MAGNET_DURATION`, `P10_SCOOP_DURATION`)
  to clear the temporary level on expiry, while leaving stored P6/P7 grants
  intact.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Needs `equipWeapon` / `_weaponTimers` /
  `getWeaponLevel` / `getWeaponLevels` to split temporary from permanent; only
  `equipWeapon(id, true)` raises the permanent level; the 10 s timeout expiry
  clears the temporary level.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — Needs `ChoiceContext` / `buildChoiceCandidates`
  to consume the **permanent** level and derive `★ New` ownership from
  permanent grants.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` — Need to supply the permanent-level
  context and keep parity.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Needs the effective-level readout.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Needs §4.4.2 / §4.4.3 updated to describe
  the temporary/permanent split and consumable-grant persistence.

## Related work

- `related-to:AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J` — Weapon leveling (epic that introduced
  persistent weapon levels).
- `related-to:AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV` — Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling.
- `related-to:AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6` — Design level curves for all power-ups.
- `related-to:AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K` — Wire power-up level curves into
  EffectsRegistry and the shared effect path (single mutation point).
- `related-to:AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9` — Integrate power-up level-up offers into the
  hold-full choice.
- `related-to:AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L` / `related-to:AH-0MUTPEHMP0074Y1L` — P9/P10
  hybrid timed-pickup / permanent-stack semantics.
- `discovered-from` follow-up: [Consider a distinct power-up type for
  consumable temporary grants (P6/P7) (AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN)] — non-blocking
  exploration of the producer's "second power-up type" suggestion.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** – Integrate power-up level-up offers into the hold-full choice (completed)
- **AH-0MUTPEKNU000AFHR** – Documentation and full project test suite validation for P10 (completed)
- **AH-0MUQUC14P006F6SH** – F1: AOE core infrastructure (descriptor + dispatch) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mupmpcb2009j54j, 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0muv5clvo002zhs9, 0muv5clw6005vf7k, ac3 (+256 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mupmpcb2009j54j, 0mutotlcy005nz8l, 0mutpehmp0074y1l, 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0muv5clvo002zhs9 (+251 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5, active (+207 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- Q1: "Unconsumed consumable grants (P6 Phase Shift charges / P7 Teleport
  stacks) when a temporary window expires — should temporary-granted,
  still-unused grants disappear at expiry?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive): **(b) persist until consumed** — once a
  charge/teleport is in hand it stays usable even after the level reverts. The
  producer also asked us to *consider creating a second power-up type* for
  this consumable-grant distinction; captured as non-blocking follow-up
  AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN. Source: interactive reply, session
  `herdr-1791324139-3250314-7031`.
- Q2: "The `★ New` badge in the hold-full choice for a field-only item (never
  permanently granted) — should a field pickup count as ownership?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive): **(a) permanent grants only** — ownership
  derives from `permanentGrants`, so the item still reads `★ New` until
  permanently acquired. Source: interactive reply, session
  `herdr-1791324139-3250314-7031`.
- Q3: "Temporary window duration per weapon/power-up — reuse existing
  timed-effect durations, or a new uniform window?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive): **(a) reuse existing durations** — weapons
  `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s), power-ups their configured duration (e.g. P3
  shield 15 s), refreshed on each new field pickup. Source: interactive reply,
  session `herdr-1791324139-3250314-7031`.


## Resolved decision 4 (planning)

**Temporary window for power-ups with no existing timed effect (P4 bomb snap, P6 phase charges, P7 teleport stacks, P8 lives).**

Resolved: **(c) no temporary window.** These power-ups apply their effect (P4 single explosion, P6 charges, P7 teleports, P8 lives) immediately at the effective level on pickup, and their temporary level component is **not** tied to a timed window — it persists for the run and is cleared only on run reset (`reset()` / `resetPowerUpLevels()`). Timed temporary windows apply only to power-ups whose effect is already timed — **P3 (shield, 15 s), P5 (speed, 10 s), P9 (magnet, 15 s), P10 (scoop, 15 s)** — and to **weapons** (`WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS`, 10 s).

Consequence: for P4/P6/P7/P8 a field pickup raises `tempStacks` for the remainder of the run (no expiry revert); the permanent/temporary distinction still governs the hold-full choice (ownership and offered level derive from `permanentGrants` only), and run reset clears both. This is a deliberate, documented narrowing of AC1 for instant/consumable power-ups, chosen to avoid a new balance constant and keep instant grants simple. Non-blocking follow-up AH-0MUX93S6F005LLXN covers the producer's distinct-consumable-power-up-type idea; it is out of scope here.

Source: producer reply in planning session `herdr-1791326409-3306860-31843` (Q1 → c).

## Plan: feature breakdown

| # | Feature | Type | Priority | Depends on |
|---|---------|------|----------|------------|
| F1 | Temporary/permanent level contract tests | task | critical | — |
| F2 | Power-up temporary/permanent split | feature | high | F1 |
| F3 | Weapon temporary/permanent split | feature | high | F1 |
| F4 | Choice and HUD consume permanent/effective levels | feature | high | F1, F2, F3 |
| F5 | Gym↔game parity and run-restart integration | feature | high | F2, F3, F4 |
| F6 | Documentation for temporary/permanent level split | docs | medium | F2, F3, F4, F5 |
| F7 | Full test-suite verification | task | high | F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6 |

All 11 parent acceptance criteria are covered by the children (automated AC-coverage review: 100%, recommendation `proceed`). Test-first ordering: F1 (tests) precedes implementation; F7 verifies the full suite.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers (planning)

- Q4: "Temporary window for power-ups with no existing timed effect (P4 bomb snap, P6 phase charges, P7 teleport stacks, P8 lives) — Resolved decision 3 says reuse existing timed-effect durations, but these have none. Which window should expire their temporary level?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(c) no temporary window** — their grants apply immediately and persist; the temporary level is cleared only on run reset. Timed temporary windows apply only to P3/P5/P9/P10 and weapons. Source: producer reply in planning session `herdr-1791326409-3306860-31843`. This narrows AC1 for instant/consumable power-ups and is recorded as Resolved decision 4 above.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-06 — Plan skill decomposed this critical bug into 7 child features (F1–F7) with dependency edges, recorded Resolved decision 4 (Q1 → no temporary window for P4/P6/P7/P8) and planning Appendix Q4, and advanced the stage to `plan_complete`. Automated review: six stages completed; AC-coverage review 100% (`proceed`).

# Epic: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

## Problem

The shipped attract/demo bot (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ and its follow-ups) is a
per-frame priority ladder with a reaction-time governor bolted on. It has no
commitment, no forward model, no aim/fire reasoning and no way to learn from
human play, so it reads as random and cannot be tuned into competence. We need
a **maintainable bot framework** that plays competently and human-like, adapts
to new content (enemies, power-ups, weapons) without a rewrite, can be re-run
headless for reproducible evaluation, and is backed by **telemetry** gathered
both from our own recordings and from production playtesters.

## Goals / user stories

- **As the maintainer**, I can re-run the bot headless on a fixed seed and get
  reproducible results, so I can improve it safely.
- **As the maintainer**, I can add a new enemy / power-up / weapon and have the
  bot handle it through configuration, without touching the core.
- **As the maintainer**, I can record human play and analyse it (reaction
  times, target choices, engagement distances, dodge behaviour) to tune and
  evaluate the bot.
- **As the maintainer**, I can enable opt-in telemetry in production and gather
  playtester data (state + input + events) to improve the bot and the game.
- **As a player**, I see an attract/demo mode that looks like a competent
  player.

## Design overview

- **Determinism.** A per-run **seed** drives all gameplay RNG (wave/spawn/
  timing) so a run is reproducible and the bot can be evaluated same-seed.
- **Telemetry.** A **versioned, consent-gated, pluggable** pipeline. Records
  are per-tick state + input + discrete events, tagged with the run seed and a
  schema version. Sinks: a local JSONL dev sink and a production remote sink.
  No PII; **disabled by default in production**, opt-in only.
- **Bot framework.** A world model (from `BotSnapshot`), a **registry of
  goals/behaviours**, a **utility selector with commitment/hysteresis**, a
  behaviour-tree executor, and predictive **dodge/aim** behaviours.
  Content-specific parameters live in a **config/registry** so new content is
  data, not code.
- **Evaluation.** Same-seed bot-vs-human runs, metrics, A/B comparisons and
  side-by-side clips.
- **Style matching (later).** Fit parameters or train a policy from recorded
  telemetry once the competent bot exists.

## Epic acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** Runs are reproducible from a seed; the seed is recorded in
  telemetry; a headless runner executes the bot for N ticks on a seed and
  produces a deterministic report.
- **AC2:** Telemetry is a pluggable framework with a documented, versioned
  schema, disabled by default in production and opt-in consent-gated; it
  records per-tick state + input + events with the seed and is a no-op when
  disabled.
- **AC3:** The bot is a structured framework (world model + goal/behaviour
  registry + committed selection + predictive dodge/aim), not a per-frame
  priority ladder; new enemies/power-ups/weapons are handled via config with
  tests.
- **AC4:** The competent bot completes representative runs with human-like
  behaviour (goal commitment, no suicide, human cadence) and passes an
  evaluation report (survival, minerals/min, targets engaged, dodges).
- **AC5:** Human play can be recorded and analysed offline, and a replay/ghost
  viewer compares bot vs human on the same seed.
- **AC6:** Production telemetry can be enabled by a playtester via an explicit
  opt-in, with privacy documentation and no PII.
- **AC7:** All documentation is updated (framework, extension guide, telemetry
  schema/privacy); full suite, typecheck and build pass.

## Out of scope (this epic)

- A fully style-matched clone of a specific player (style matching is an
  early-phase deliverable; full fidelity is a later follow-up).
- Server-side ML training infrastructure or online multiplayer.
- CI wiring of the capture/eval jobs (follow-up once the harness exists).

## Children (dependency order)

1. Deterministic run seeding + seed plumbing.
2. Telemetry framework (versioned schema, pluggable sinks, consent flag).
3. Game telemetry instrumentation (per-tick state + events).
4. Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling.
5. Bot framework core (world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy,
   content config).
6. Structured competent bot (utility goals + behaviour tree + predictive
   dodge/aim).
7. Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons.
8. Same-seed evaluation harness (metrics, A/B, side-by-side clips).
9. Style matching from telemetry (parameter fitting / imitation).
10. Production telemetry (opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink, docs).

## Related work

Builds on AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ (Smart capture bot) and its follow-ups
AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB (human-like input) and AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L (movement
goals). Supersedes the per-frame priority-ladder design.
data.title: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

## Summary
Dev tooling to record a human session, analyse it offline and replay/ghost it against the bot — the data loop for tuning and evaluating the bot.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A dev command/mode records a human session to JSONL (state + input + events + seed) using the telemetry framework.
- AC2: An offline analysis script produces a report: key-hold duration histogram, input-change cadence, reaction latency proxy, target-choice stats (mineral/power-up/enemy), engagement distances, dodge outcomes, survival/minerals-per-minute.
- AC3: A replay/ghost viewer steps a recording deterministically and overlays human vs bot input/position (same seed).
- AC4: The recorded dataset is versioned and documented so scripts can evolve with the schema.
- AC5: Tests for the analyser (pure stats) and the replay stepping.
- AC6: Docs: how to record, analyse and replay.
data.title: Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling

data.description:
## Summary
Implement the **competent** structured bot on top of the framework: utility-based goal selection with commitment, behaviour-tree execution (seek → line up → engage/collect → dodge), explicit aim/fire reasoning and predictive dodging. Competent first; style matching comes later.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: Goal set covering the operator's order (minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids) plus survival, each as a registered goal with a utility/priority and hysteresis.
- AC2: Behaviours: collect (approach + scoop), engage enemy, engage asteroid, evade (predictive path-around, not just direction rejection), reposition/idle.
- AC3: **Aim/fire reasoning**: the bot positions to line up a target while dodging, rather than only aiming by accident of movement.
- AC4: Survival is a hard constraint: never-suicide property tests over sampled snapshots; no wall/enemy/bullet/asteroid collision when a safe alternative exists.
- AC5: Human-like cadence: committed input changes no faster than the human-like toggles; tunables single-sourced.
- AC6: The competent bot completes a representative run (survives/destroys enough) and beats the old ladder on an evaluation metric.
- AC7: Deterministic unit tests per goal/behaviour; integration test on a seeded run.
- AC8: Docs updated (the new decision model).
data.title: Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour tree, predictive dodge/aim

data.description:
## Summary
Make the bot **content-adaptive**: new enemies, power-ups and weapons should be handled via configuration, not core changes, so the bot keeps working as the game grows.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A content config/registry describes, per enemy archetype, threat value, preferred engagement range, aim/lead behaviour and whether it is an asteroid-like hazard.
- AC2: Power-up and weapon definitions declare bot-relevant value/priority (e.g. collection desirability) consumed by the goal scorer.
- AC3: Adding a new enemy/power-up/weapon requires only a config entry (plus its game data) — demonstrated by a test that registers a synthetic content type and the bot handles it.
- AC4: Unknown content degrades gracefully (documented default).
- AC5: Unit tests for the config lookup and the synthetic-content path.
- AC6: Docs: "how to teach the bot about new content".
data.title: Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons

data.description:
## Summary
A reproducible evaluation harness: run the bot (and replay a human recording) on the same seed, produce metrics, A/B two bot versions, and render side-by-side clips. This is how we "re-run the bot production code" after changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A headless runner executes the bot for N ticks/seeds and emits a deterministic report (from telemetry).
- AC2: Same-seed comparison: bot vs human recording, and bot-vs-bot across versions, with metrics (survival time, minerals/min, power-ups, enemies/asteroids destroyed, avoidable hits, input cadence).
- AC3: A/B runner compares two bot configs/versions and reports the difference with confidence (multiple seeds).
- AC4: Optional side-by-side video via the existing capture tooling.
- AC5: Results are reproducible (same seed + config → same report) and stored as artifacts.
- AC6: Tests for the runner/report (pure aggregation) and determinism.
- AC7: Docs: how to run evaluations and interpret the report.
data.title: Same-seed evaluation harness: metrics, A/B, side-by-side

data.description:
## Summary
Later phase: make the bot **match a player's style** using recorded telemetry (parameter fitting and/or behaviour cloning), on top of the competent framework.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A pipeline that extracts style features from human recordings (reaction latency, hold distribution, target preferences, engagement distances, risk appetite).
- AC2: A parameter-fitting path that maps those features onto the structured bot's tunables (preferred first; keeps safety guarantees).
- AC3: (Optional/stretch) A behaviour-cloning policy trained from `(state → input)` pairs, evaluated against the structured bot on the same seeds.
- AC4: Evaluation shows the styled bot is measurably closer to the human recording than the default competent bot, without regressing competence/survival.
- AC5: Docs: how to train/fit and evaluate a style.
- AC6: Tests for the feature extraction (pure).

## Notes
Depends on the recording/analysis tooling and the evaluation harness. Lower priority than competence.
data.title: Style matching from telemetry (parameter fitting / imitation)

## Summary
Turn on telemetry in **production** for playtesters: an explicit opt-in consent flow, privacy-safe records, batched upload to a remote sink, and documentation.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: An in-game consent/opt-in prompt (and a settings toggle) gating production telemetry; default **off**; easy opt-out.
- AC2: A remote sink that batches and uploads records (endpoint configurable), with retry/backoff and no gameplay impact when offline.
- AC3: Records are PII-free and documented; a data-retention/privacy note is included in the docs and (if applicable) the consent screen.
- AC4: A remote-off/no-op path so local dev and offline play are unaffected (tests).
- AC5: A simple way to inspect downloaded telemetry (reuse the analysis tooling from child 4).
- AC6: Tests for consent gating, the uploader's batching/backoff, and the disabled path.
- AC7: Docs: telemetry privacy + how playtester data is stored and used.
data.title: Production telemetry: opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink

# Remove PowerUpType and unify dispatch on PowerUpId

## Summary
Delete the duplicate `PowerUpType` enum and the `PowerUpEntry.type` field so a
single identifier (`PowerUpId`) drives the catalogue, effect dispatch, icon
lookup and the effects registry.

## User story
As a maintainer, I want one identifier per power-up so there is no second
`PowerUpType` union that can drift out of sync with the ID union.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `PowerUpType` no longer exists anywhere under `src/`, and `PowerUpEntry`
   carries no `type` field.
2. Effect dispatch (`src/powerups/effects.ts`), icon/colour lookup
   (`src/powerups/icons.ts`), the effects registry and `getPowerUpById` all key
   off `PowerUpId`; helper signatures (`drawPowerUpIcon`, `drawPowerUpDrop`,
   etc.) updated accordingly.
3. Tests asserting `PowerUpEntry.type` or `PowerUpType` are updated; new or
   updated tests cover the unified dispatch path (catalogue -> effect and
   catalogue -> icon colour for all eight IDs).
4. No duplicate union of power-up identifiers remains; `npm run typecheck`
   and the full test suite pass.

### Parent AC coverage (AH-0MUX6S20F002GHPF)

- **Single identifier.** The separate `PowerUpType` enum is removed; effect dispatch, icon lookup, the effects registry and `PowerUpEntry` all key off `PowerUpId` (the redundant per-entry `type` field is dropped). No duplicate union of power-up identifiers remains.

## Minimal implementation
- Remove `PowerUpType` from `src/powerups/types.ts` and the `.type` field from
  catalogue entries and `PowerUpEntry`.
- Switch `effects.ts` dispatch on `entry.id` (values already read as English);
  update the `EffectsRegistry` maps and helper `type` parameters to
  `PowerUpId`.
- Re-key `ICON_COLORS` in `icons.ts` on `PowerUpId`; update switch statements
  and bubble-colour helpers.
- Update tests that construct entries with `type:` or assert `PowerUpType.*`.

## Dependencies
- F2 (name-valued `PowerUpId`) — required before the enum can be deleted.

## Deliverables
- Removed `PowerUpType` enum and `.type` field.
- `PowerUpId`-keyed dispatch/icon/registry code and updated tests.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Remove `PowerUpType`, `PowerUpEntry.type`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Dispatch on `PowerUpId`.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — `ICON_COLORS`/switch keyed on `PowerUpId`.
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/icons.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts` — Update fixtures.
- `src/test/powerUpEffectFixtures.ts` — Update effect fixtures.

# Migrate persisted powerUpWeights to name keys

## Summary
Bump `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` and translate a stored legacy P-keyed
`powerUpWeights` table to the new name keys in `loadRules()`, so customised
drop weights survive the rename (localStorage key `ai-hell-game-rules`).

## User story
As a player with tuned spawn weights, I want my customised drop weights to
survive the upgrade so the rename does not silently reset my configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped from `3` to `4`.
2. `loadRules()` migrates a stored legacy `powerUpWeights` table from the
   `P3`-`P10` keys to the equivalent name keys; unknown or non-numeric keys are
   still ignored; partial tables are still merged over defaults; an
   already-name-keyed config is unchanged.
3. A regression test proves a version-3 config with a customised P-keyed
   weight (for example `P8: 9`) loads under the equivalent name key
   (`extra_life: 9`) with every other rule preserved, and that a version-4
   name-keyed config round-trips unchanged.
4. `saveRules()` persists name-keyed weights with `version: 4`; the existing
   version-1/2 mineral-hold and re-drop migrations are unchanged.

### Parent AC coverage (AH-0MUX6S20F002GHPF)

- **Persisted rules migrate.** `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped and `loadRules()` migrates a stored legacy `powerUpWeights` table from the `P3`–`P10` keys to the new name keys, so customised drop weights survive the upgrade. A regression test proves a version-3 config with customised P-keyed weights loads under the equivalent name keys.

## Minimal implementation
- Add a `LEGACY_POWER_UP_ID_BY_CODE` map (`P3` -> `shield`, ... `P10` ->
  `mineral_scoop`) in `src/core/rules.ts`.
- Extend `mergeWeights(stored)` (or add a migration pass keyed on
  `parsed.version < 4`) to translate legacy keys before merging.
- Bump `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 4 and document the migration in the version
  comment.
- Add the regression tests to `src/core/rules.test.ts`.

## Dependencies
- F2 (name-valued `PowerUpId`) — the name keys must exist first.

## Deliverables
- Schema-version bump + legacy weight migration.
- Version-3 regression test and version-4 round-trip test.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `src/core/rules.ts` — `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `mergeWeights`, migration map.
- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — v3 migration + v4 round-trip regression tests.
data.title: Migrate persisted powerUpWeights to name keys

data.comment:
HUD rework (addresses producer rejection) — Session ID: herdr-1791378090-732397-12839.

The rejection asked for one entry per power-up/weapon showing the current level plus an infinity/timer indicator. Implemented in the shared src/ui/HUD.ts (game + all gyms consume the same HUD):

- Rows are now merged: a power-up/weapon gets exactly ONE row even when it has both a permanent level and an active temporary field window (previously P9/P10/P6 could emit two rows — e.g. a permanent stack row plus a timed row).
- Label carries the current effective level (permanent + temporary), e.g. 'Speed Boost Lvl 3' / 'Weapon: spread Lvl 3'.
- Value column is strictly the producer's spec: '∞' when no temporary level-up window is active (the level is permanent for the run), or a live 'Ns' countdown while a temporary window is active.
- Consumable resources the level alone does not convey (P3 remaining absorptions, P6 charges, P7 teleports) are shown as a ' ×N' suffix in the label so the value column stays strictly ∞/countdown and no gameplay information is lost.

Supporting changes:
- EffectsRegistry: new powerUpLevel()/powerUpTemporaryRemaining() accessors feed the merged row model; weapon effects now carry a tempWindow flag so a field pickup on top of a permanent weapon shows a countdown that reverts to ∞ (previously permanent weapons showed a misleading '10s' and never counted down).
- Docs updated (GDD §4.4.2/§4.4.3 HUD presentation notes, README HUD/effects entries).

Assumption recorded: the value column is reserved for ∞/countdown per the producer's wording, with consumable counts moved into the label. If the producer prefers the counts elsewhere, that is a small follow-up.
